# Feature: Execution History

## 1. Feature Goal

**ID**: FEAT-110
**Source Plan**: `.spec-lite/plan_mvp.md`

Every earlier row creates a record, but nothing yet lets a person find it again. FEAT-103 persists every conversation event with a gap-free `seq`. FEAT-104 keeps each input byte-for-byte. FEAT-105 keeps the exact text a person approved and a receipt for every send. FEAT-106 keeps every code version by digest. FEAT-107 binds each check to code and runtime, and each run to an approval. FEAT-109 turns output files into owned artifacts. All of it survives a restart. None of it can be found again: `/history` is still FEAT-101's placeholder ("Execution history arrives in FEAT-110."), the task page shows only `executions.at(-1)`, and no route deletes anything. This row makes the record usable.

Concretely:

- **One row per task, newest run first.** `/history` lists every task once: its name, its latest run's state in plain English, when that run started, how many runs it has had, and how many outputs the latest run produced. A person can search over their own words and filter by **Needs you**, **Running**, **Done**, or **Didn't finish**. Runs parked on the person (a question, an approval, a review) collect in a strip at the top, because a run whose gate nobody can find never finishes.
- **A task is a timeline of runs, and each run is a record.** Opening a task shows what was asked, which files were attached, and every run: the first run, a retry with the person's guidance, a re-run after they said the result was wrong. Each is labelled with why it exists and quotes what the person said. Opening a run shows its transcript, its outputs (with downloads), and a provenance summary: what was sent and to whom, what was asked, which code version ran (by digest), what the checks found and on which runtime, who approved it, and how it ended. Each summary line opens the component the owning feature already built. This row composes those components; it does not re-render their data.
- **Delete means delete.** Deleting a task removes every row it owns (by cascade) *and* every file it owns (by name). That covers `uploads/{taskId}/` and `artifacts/{taskId}/`, plus three trees nothing removes today: `runs/{executionId}/`, `scripts/{executionId}/`, and `agent-sessions/{executionId}/`. The last holds the raw provider log, including every prompt the model saw. `runs/{executionId}/input/` holds a full copy of the person's file. A deleted task that left those behind would be a false promise the person has no way to detect. A test deletes the only task, then asserts that every task-owned table is empty and every tree is gone.
- **Restarts and disconnects have defined outcomes.** FEAT-103 made reconnect resume from `lastSeq` and made a restart interrupt live runs. FEAT-107 made approvals and reviews survive a restart. This row fixes the one case where the specs disagree (see *Restart partition* below). It gives every non-terminal state a stated restart outcome, enforced by a partition test. It distinguishes "the app was closed" from "you cancelled". It offers **Run again** wherever a run was interrupted.

For the person running the preview: they come back after lunch, open History, see *"Waiting for your go-ahead — Monthly sales summary"* at the top, click it, and approve. They find last week's report and download it again. They delete a test task, and it disappears from the disk as well as the screen.

### Decisions applied (resolved 2026-09-24)

The plan lists FEAT-110 as blocked by **D10** (server-owned state, WS progress and recovery, loopback-only access, local session protection without accounts) and **D12** (retention of inputs and provenance). Earlier rows resolved parts of both for their own scope: FEAT-103 settled D10's state ownership, transport, and loopback-plus-Origin access; FEAT-104 settled input retention; FEAT-109 settled output retention. The remaining parts were resolved with the user before this spec was written. They are recorded here because `plan_mvp.md` §5 still lists D10 and D12 as open. Each resolution applies to *this row* only.

| Decision | Resolution | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| History unit (product fork) | **One row per task.** A task appears once, carrying its latest run's state. Opening it shows every run as a timeline. Runs waiting on the person get their own strip at the top of the page. | The alternative was one row per run, which lists a task retried three times as three rows. With FEAT-106's guidance retry and FEAT-107's feedback re-run, retries are a normal part of a task's life, and grouping them is what makes "the report from last week" findable. This decision depends on *one open run per task* (Assumptions), and TASK-003 enforces that. |
| D12 — deletion scope | **Whole tasks only.** There is no per-run delete, and (per FEAT-109) no per-artifact delete. | This keeps the retention rule FEAT-104 and FEAT-109 already use: everything lives for the life of the task. Deleting a task is the only way anything leaves, and it removes all of it. FEAT-106's `ON DELETE SET NULL` on `retry_of_execution_id` stays as it is. It is harmless, and it will support per-run delete if that is ever approved. Queued in TODO.md. |
| D12 — provenance retention | **Life of the task, for everything.** This covers the transcript, disclosure consents and receipts, clarifications, code versions and fixtures, verification results, approvals, run `stdout`/`stderr`, artifacts, the run directory with its input copy, and the raw agent session log. All of it is deleted with the task and never purged by age. | One retention rule now covers the whole pipeline: FEAT-104's rule for inputs, FEAT-109's for outputs, and this row's for everything in between. It resolves TODO.md's two open D12 items (disclosure records, `conversation_event`) and its `runs/` retention item with the same answer. The cost is unbounded growth, which is real and already tracked as the storage-quota item. That is a question of size; this decision is about lifetime. Two alternatives were rejected: deleting each run's input copy when the run settles, and purging session logs by age. They are recorded here so nobody has to re-derive them. |
| D10 — local session protection | **Origin/Host guard on the one new write route. Reads rely on the same-origin policy. The per-install token stays a pre-pilot item.** `DELETE /api/tasks/:taskId` gets FEAT-103's `originGuard`. The three new `GET`s get none. A test asserts that no `/api` response ever carries an `Access-Control-Allow-*` header, and that every `/api` JSON response carries `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`. | A cross-site page can make the browser *send* a GET to `127.0.0.1`, but it cannot *read* the response without a CORS header, and this application never sets one. That is what protects a listable collection of prompts and filenames, so the test asserts it rather than assuming it. A token would also block other OS accounts and local processes. In this preview, though, generated code already runs unisolated under the person's own account and can read `data/automate.db` directly, so a token adds little today. TODO.md's pre-pilot D10 item stays open. |
| D10 — list liveness (design fork) | **Poll; add no new socket channel.** The history list and the run timeline refetch every 5 s while any visible run is in the running group, and also on window focus and on network reconnect. An open run page keeps FEAT-103's socket. | FEAT-103's socket is per-execution and ordered by `seq`. A list-wide channel would need either a second ordering authority or unsequenced "something changed" pings, and the client would re-fetch on those anyway. One indexed query every 5 s, and only while something is running, is cheaper than either and cannot drift out of sync. |
| Restart partition (spec conflict) | **A restart interrupts `waiting`. `awaiting_approval` and `awaiting_review` survive it.** Every non-terminal status belongs to exactly one of `INTERRUPTED_ON_RESTART` and `SURVIVES_RESTART`, and a partition test asserts it. | **DEVIATION — awaiting confirmation.** FEAT-105 §1 says a restart interrupts a `waiting` run: *"The promise is in-memory: a restart loses it, reconciliation marks the execution interrupted, and the persisted answers make the retry cheap."* FEAT-107 TASK-004 narrows `listActive()` so that reconciliation skips all three parked statuses. Memory's Architecture section says both things: parked statuses *"hold no in-memory state, so they survive a restart"*, and, in the D06 entry, *"a restart-interrupted run re-seeds them"*. They cannot both hold. FEAT-105 has the facts right. `request_clarification` holds a live Pi session open on an in-memory promise, so after a restart there is nothing left for an answer to resolve. A `waiting` row that survived would sit in **Needs you** forever, accepting answers that go nowhere. Approvals and reviews are database rows, not promises, so they genuinely survive. The fix separates two properties that FEAT-107's `PARKED_STATUSES` combined: *holds no concurrency slot* (true for all three) and *survives a restart* (true for two). It is recorded in TODO.md so FEAT-107's implementation can adopt it directly. TASK-003 enforces it however FEAT-107 lands. |

### Assumptions carried (flag if wrong)

- **FEAT-105 through FEAT-109 are implemented before this row.** Plan order and dependency order agree. At the time of writing only FEAT-101–104 exist in code, so every reference to a later table, repository, route, or component points to that feature's **spec**, and TASK-002's queries use column names from those specs' §2. Where an implementation diverges from its spec, the implementation wins and the query follows it.
- **History composes other features' views; it never re-renders their data.** The run record returns a one-line summary for each section. The detail behind each line is fetched from the owning feature's existing endpoint and rendered by that feature's own component. There is no second disclosure view, no second verification report, and no second artifact list. Two renderers of the same data drift apart. The rules for untrusted content (FEAT-103's markdown policy, FEAT-104's formula prefixes, FEAT-109's sandbox) must each live in exactly one place.
- **Runs recorded before a feature existed are still valid runs.** Such a run simply has no rows for that feature: a FEAT-103-era text-only run has no inputs, no disclosure, and no code version. Every optional section of its run record is then `null` and renders as absent, never as an error. TASK-005 tests a record built from FEAT-103's three tables alone.
- **No new state, no state-machine edge, no event kind.** History reads the state machine without changing it. The restart partition (TASK-003) classifies existing statuses and adds no transition. Deleting a task appends no event, because its transcript is deleted along with it.
- **Nothing in this row reaches a provider.** There is no session, no prompt, and no transmission, which extends FEAT-107/108/109's property to `src/history/`. **Run again** is FEAT-106's `POST /api/executions/:id/retry`, unchanged in what it sends and in how it re-checks FEAT-105's consent.
- **Each task has at most one open run.** FEAT-106's retry only requires the *source* run to be terminal. Without a further check, a person could retry an older failed run while the latest run sits at an approval gate, giving one task two open runs. "A task's state is its latest run's state" would then be false. TASK-003 makes both the retry and the feedback-retry paths refuse while the task has any non-terminal run. The history list and the delete guard both rely on this.
- **Task deletion is a service, not a repository side effect.** In FEAT-109's spec, `TaskRepository.delete` calls the artifact and upload file sweeps. This row moves that orchestration into `TaskDeletionService`: the repository deletes rows and reports what it deleted, and the service removes the files. If FEAT-109 shipped as specified, TASK-006 moves those two calls so nothing is duplicated.
- **`GET /api/tasks/:taskId` keeps its `executions` array.** FEAT-103's response returns every execution, unpaginated. The rebuilt task page stops reading it in favour of the paginated timeline (TASK-005), but removing the array would break an existing contract, and memory requires asking before dropping backwards compatibility. It stays; this row only adds a `counts` field. Dropping the array is queued in TODO.md as a question for the user.

## 2. Data Model (Granular)

`.spec-lite/data_model.md` predates the confirmed decisions and is **not** the authoritative schema (reconciliation is tracked in `.spec-lite/TODO.md`). It names the query this row serves (`idx_execution_created_at`: *"Sort executions by date (execution history page, pagination)"*) and proposes nothing else for it. That index is not adopted: execution ids are `AUTOINCREMENT` and already give creation order without timestamp ties, and epoch-second `created_at` values collide within a second.

**No new table, no new column, no new event kind.** Everything history shows is already stored by FEAT-103–109. The only schema change is one index. What this row adds to the model are two things that were implicit and are now enforced: which rows and files a task owns, and what a restart does to each status.

Conventions carried from FEAT-101–109: `snake_case` singular tables and columns; the schema defined in driver-independent `drizzle-orm/sqlite-core`; no Drizzle query outside `src/db/`.

### Entities read (not modified)

History is a **read model** over other features' tables. The table below lists every column it reads and, just as importantly, the columns it must never select.

| Table (owner) | History reads | Never selected by history |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `task` (FEAT-103) | `id`, `name`, `description` (search and header only), `created_at` | — |
| `execution` (FEAT-103, 106, 107) | `id`, `task_id`, `status`, `trigger`, `retry_of_execution_id`, `guidance`, `review_feedback`, `reviewed_at`, `provider`, `model`, `usage_*`, `error_code`, `error_message`, `started_at`, `completed_at`, `duration_ms`, `created_at` | `agent_log_path`, `agent_session_id` — the raw provider artifact never has a field that could reach the client (FEAT-103's rule) |
| `conversation_event` (FEAT-103) | `MAX(seq)` per execution; `at` of the latest `state_changed` row | `payload` — transcripts are served only by FEAT-103's replay route |
| `upload` (FEAT-104) | `id`, `task_id`, `original_filename`, `format`, `byte_size`, `sha256` | — |
| `disclosure_consent`, `disclosure_transmission` (FEAT-105) | `provider`, `model`, `granted_at`, `scope_diagnostics`; transmission count by `kind` | `payload_snapshot` — the bytes are served only by FEAT-105's route |
| `clarification`, `clarification_question` (FEAT-105) | counts by `status` and `answer_source` | `prompt_text`, `answer`, `rationale` — served only by FEAT-105's route |
| `code_version`, `generation_attempt` (FEAT-106) | the final version's `id`, `attempt`, `content_digest`, `tests_passed`; number of attempts used | `code_file.content` — served only by FEAT-106's route |
| `verification_run` (FEAT-107) | latest run's `status`, `blocking_count`, `advisory_count`, `summary`, and `runtime_detail`'s Python version, platform, and package count | findings' `message` — served only by FEAT-107's route |
| `execution_approval` (FEAT-107) | `decided_at`, `acknowledged_warnings` where `decision = 'approved'` | — |
| `script_run` (FEAT-107, 108, 109) | `status`, `exit_code`, `duration_ms`, `limit_breached`, `output_truncated`, `input_manifest` (digests only), `declared_output_count`, `produced_output_count`, `artifact_count`, `unregistered_output_count` | `stdout`, `stderr` — they can contain the person's cell values and are served only by FEAT-107's route |
| `artifact` (FEAT-109) | count per execution and per task | — |

A source scan asserts that `history-repository.ts` never mentions any column in the right-hand column. A read model is easy to widen one field at a time until it returns the person's data from a route nobody reviewed for that purpose.

### What a task owns — the deletion graph

**Rows**, removed by cascade from `task` (FEAT-101's client sets `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON`, so the cascades actually fire):

```
task
├── execution ─┬─ conversation_event
│              ├─ disclosure_transmission
│              ├─ clarification ── clarification_question
│              ├─ code_version ─── code_file
│              ├─ generation_attempt
│              ├─ synthetic_fixture
│              ├─ verification_run ── verification_check ── verification_finding
│              ├─ execution_approval
│              ├─ script_run
│              └─ artifact
├── upload ── upload_profile ── upload_column
├── disclosure_consent
└── artifact                      (FEAT-109's denormalized edge)
```

The global tables — `app_meta`, `runtime_environment`, `conversation_event_kind`, and the migrator's own table — are not task-owned and deletion never touches them.

**Files**, removed by name, because SQLite cascades do not touch the filesystem:

| Tree | Keyed by | Written by | Holds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `uploads/{taskId}/` | task | FEAT-104 | the original input files |
| `artifacts/{taskId}/` | task | FEAT-109 | registered outputs |
| `runs/{executionId}/` | execution | FEAT-107 | a full copy of each input, `output/` with `manifest.json` and anything unregistered, the `verify/` fixture and scratch space |
| `scripts/{executionId}/` | execution | FEAT-106 | every code version's files and the synthetic fixtures |
| `agent-sessions/{executionId}/` | execution | FEAT-102 | the raw provider session JSONL: every prompt the model saw, including the disclosure payload and any diagnostics |

This table becomes a constant, `TASK_OWNED_TREES` in `src/history/task-owned-trees.ts`. Deletion, the orphan sweep, and the completeness test all iterate it. The completeness test also scans the data root for any directory named after the deleted task's or executions' ids, so a future feature that writes a new per-task tree fails the test until it adds a line here.

**Unattached rows.** FEAT-104 sweeps staged uploads (`upload.task_id IS NULL`) after `AUTOMATE_STAGED_UPLOAD_TTL_HOURS`. FEAT-105 creates `disclosure_consent` rows with `task_id NULL` (a person approves, then abandons the task), and nothing ever removes them. Each one holds up to 64 KiB of the person's sample rows in `payload_snapshot`. With no task, a life-of-task rule has nothing to measure against, so these rows follow the staged-upload rule: they are approvals of exactly those staged files. TASK-007 sweeps them.

### Restart partition — `packages/core/src/conversation/execution-state.ts` (modified)

| Status | Holds a concurrency slot | On restart | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pending` | yes | **interrupted** | Its start was in memory. |
| `generating` | yes | **interrupted** | A live Pi session. |
| `verifying` | yes | **interrupted** | A checker process (FEAT-107). |
| `executing` | yes | **interrupted** | The script process (FEAT-107/108). |
| `waiting` | no | **interrupted** | An in-memory tool promise inside a live Pi session (FEAT-105). |
| `awaiting_approval` | no | survives | A database row; no process, no session. |
| `awaiting_review` | no | survives | A database row; no process, no session. |
| `completed`, `failed`, `aborted`, `rejected` | — | unchanged | Terminal. |

Exports: `INTERRUPTED_ON_RESTART` (the five), `SURVIVES_RESTART` (the two), and `INTERRUPTION_MESSAGES: Readonly<Record<InterruptedOnRestart, string>>`, one plain-English message per phase. FEAT-107's `PARKED_STATUSES` and `consumesConcurrencySlot` are unchanged: they answer the *slot* question, which is a different question from what survives a restart.

### Indexes & Constraints

- `execution_active` (FEAT-103; FEAT-107 kept its five-status predicate) — **unchanged, and now correctly aligned.** Its predicate equals `INTERRUPTED_ON_RESTART`, and `ExecutionRepository.listActive()` again selects exactly that set, which reverts FEAT-107's narrowing (the restart-partition deviation). SQLite matches partial-index predicates by their text, so the schema builds the `IN` list from the core constant rather than typing it out, and a test asserts the list stored in `sqlite_master.sql` equals the constant.
- `execution_parked` (FEAT-107: `awaiting_approval`, `awaiting_review`) — **widened to `PARKED_STATUSES`**, adding `waiting`. FEAT-107 created this index *"for the 'what is waiting for me?' query FEAT-110 will want"*, and a question waiting for an answer is waiting on the person just as an approval is. The migration drops and recreates it; no table rebuild. `ExecutionRepository.listParked()` follows the new predicate (a **DEVIATION** from FEAT-107 TASK-004's "excludes `waiting`", for the reason above). The **Needs you** query uses this index, and an `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` test asserts it.
- `execution_task_id` (FEAT-103) — the list query's "is there a later run?" check and the timeline's range scan both use it. An `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` test asserts this too, because the list's cost depends on it.
- **No new constraint.** The following invariants are enforced in code and asserted in tests:
  - **One open run per task.** No task has two executions outside `TERMINAL_STATUSES` (TASK-003).
  - **Every task has at least one execution.** `createWithExecution` is the only production path that creates a task, and the list is driven from executions, so a task with no execution would not appear. A test creates tasks through every production path (`POST /api/tasks`, retry, feedback re-run) and asserts that the list count equals the task count.
  - **Deletion is complete.** After a task is deleted, no row in any task-owned table and no entry in any task-owned tree refers to it (TASK-006).
  - **History selects no protected column** (the source scan described above).

### Migration

One migration, following FEAT-109's (the specs' ordinal `0008`; drizzle-kit names the folder `drizzle/<timestamp>_<slug>/`, as the three existing folders show). It drops `execution_parked` and recreates it with the `PARKED_STATUSES` predicate. It changes no table and no data. TASK-002's migration test seeds executions in every status, applies it, and asserts that every row is untouched and the new predicate is in `sqlite_master`.

### Storage layout

No new directories. For the first time, every tree under the data root has a documented owner and a documented deletion rule:

```
~/.automate/                                   (or $AUTOMATE_HOME)
├── data/automate.db                           — rows: deleted by cascade from task
├── uploads/staged/                            — unattached: FEAT-104 TTL sweep
├── uploads/{taskId}/                          — task-owned  ┐
├── artifacts/{taskId}/                        — task-owned  │  removed by TaskDeletionService,
├── runs/{executionId}/                        — task-owned  │  and by the orphan sweep if a
├── scripts/{executionId}/                     — task-owned  │  deletion was interrupted
├── agent-sessions/{executionId}/              — task-owned  ┘
├── agent-sessions/{agent-smoke,connection-test-*}/ — not task-owned; never touched (non-numeric)
├── env/ , verify-env/                         — global runtime (FEAT-108)
└── config/ , pi/                              — global configuration (FEAT-102)
```

## 4. Dependencies

- **FEAT-101** — required: `AppPaths` and `resolveWithin`, the Drizzle/`node:sqlite` client and in-process migrator, the repository pattern, the error envelope and correlation id, the Pino logger and its redaction, TanStack Router/Query and the typed API client, the `ds.*` tokens and `check-design-tokens.mjs`, and the **History** nav link that has pointed at a placeholder since FEAT-101.
- **FEAT-102** — required: `AppPaths.sessionDirFor(executionId)` and the `agent-sessions/` layout. Deletion must remove the raw session log, and the sweep must leave the non-numeric `agent-smoke` and `connection-test-*` directories alone.
- **FEAT-103** — required and load-bearing: `task`, `execution`, `conversation_event`; the state machine and `isTerminal`; `TaskSessionRegistry` with `reconcileOnStartup`, `drain`, and `abort`; `useExecutionStream` and the replay route; `originGuard`; every conversation component, which `run-view.tsx` extracts unchanged.
- **FEAT-104** — required: `upload` and its sweep, `UploadFileStore.removeTaskDirectory`, `AUTOMATE_STAGED_UPLOAD_TTL_HOURS`, `GET /api/tasks/:taskId/uploads`, and the profile preview components the inputs list links to.
- **FEAT-105** — required: `disclosure_consent`, `disclosure_transmission`, `clarification`, `clarification_question`, their routes and components (the record panel opens them), `priorAnswersForTask` (which makes **Run again** after an interrupted `waiting` run painless), and the consent repository this row extends.
- **FEAT-106** — required: `code_version`, `generation_attempt`, `synthetic_fixture`, `execution.retry_of_execution_id` and `guidance`, `createRetry`, `POST /api/executions/:id/retry` (**Run again**), `scripts/{executionId}/`, and the code-version components.
- **FEAT-107** — required: the full status union, `TERMINAL_STATUSES`, `PARKED_STATUSES`, `consumesConcurrencySlot`, the `execution_parked` index (widened here), `listParked`, `createFeedbackRetry`, `verification_run`, `execution_approval`, `script_run`, `runs/{executionId}/`, and the verification, intent, run-result, and review components.
- **FEAT-108** — required: `script_run.limit_breached` and `describeLimitBreach` (the record's run line uses its wording, never a second one).
- **FEAT-109** — required: `artifact`, `ArtifactRepository.countByTask`, `deleteTaskArtifacts` and its orphan sweep, `artifact-list.tsx`, and the archive route. Together these are "access to prior outputs in execution history", which the plan keeps in scope after D08 deferred the standalone library.
- **External**: **none new.** Relative times use `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat`. The confirmation dialog is built on plain elements with ARIA roles. Pages of 20 need no virtualization library.

### Not dependencies (deliberately)

- **FEAT-111.** No templates, no "run against another file", no input mapping. **Run again** re-runs a task on its own inputs through FEAT-106's existing route.
- **A search index (FTS5).** Search is a bounded `LIKE` over task names and prompts, paged. Whether this `node:sqlite` build ships FTS5 was not verified, and a person's history is small enough that a keyset scan finishes in milliseconds. Queued in TODO.md for revisiting if history grows.
- **A list-wide WebSocket channel.** See the list-liveness decision.
- **A dialog, date, or virtualization library.** Each would be a new dependency in the one screen that lists all of a person's work.
- **A provider session.** No model call anywhere in this row.

### TASK-002: The history read model — `HistoryRepository` and the index migration

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - **`listTasks({ cursor, limit, group, q })`.** Add `packages/server/src/db/repositories/history-repository.ts`. The page is **driven from executions**. It selects each task's latest execution, meaning an execution with no later sibling (`NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM execution later WHERE later.task_id = e.task_id AND later.id > e.id)`, served by `execution_task_id`). It joins `task`, applies `e.id < :cursor`, the group's status list (always built from `HISTORY_STATUS_GROUPS`, never typed), and the search predicate, orders by `e.id DESC`, and fetches `limit + 1` rows to compute `hasMore`.
    - The cursor is the last item's latest-run id. Execution ids are `AUTOINCREMENT`, so ordering is "most recently started run first", free of the one-second ties `created_at` would produce. A task given a new run moves to the top instead of reshuffling later pages.
    - Search uses `LIKE ? ESCAPE '\'` over `task.name` and `task.description`, after escaping `\`, `%`, and `_` in the term, so the term is literal text and cannot act as a pattern. Case folding is ASCII-only, which is SQLite's `LIKE` behavior; this is documented rather than hidden.
    - Counts for a page come from three grouped queries keyed by the page's ids: runs per task, uploads per task, and artifacts on each latest run. A fourth reads each latest run's last `state_changed` `at` for `statusSince`. **A page costs five queries whatever its size**; the test counts them.
  - **`listRuns(taskId, { cursor, limit })`.** Newest first, keyset on `id`, through `execution_task_id`, with per-run artifact counts and `guidance IS NOT NULL` / `review_feedback IS NOT NULL` flags. The text itself is returned only by the record.
  - **`getRunRecord(executionId)`.** One small query per section, each against an execution-keyed index, reading only the columns in §2's table. It returns a raw struct, and `src/history/presenters.ts` maps it to `RunRecord`:
    - `chain.previous` comes from `retry_of_execution_id`; `chain.next` from rows whose `retry_of_execution_id` is this id.
    - `inputs` comes from the task's uploads. `inputsReadByRun` is `null` when no `script_run` exists; otherwise it is true only when every `input_manifest` entry's `sha256` equals its upload's. This makes "this run read exactly these files" a comparison between two stored facts.
    - `checks.runtime` becomes one line (*"Python 3.12.4 on win32 · 8 packages"*).
    - Digests are shortened to 12 characters for display, and the full value stays available.
  - **`taskCounts(taskId)`.** Returns `{ runs, inputs, outputs, openRunId }`.
  - **Schema and migration.** In `schema.ts`, build `execution_parked`'s predicate from `PARKED_STATUSES` and `execution_active`'s from `INTERRUPTED_ON_RESTART`, then generate the migration. Only `execution_parked` changes; confirm by reading the generated SQL that it is a `DROP INDEX` / `CREATE INDEX` and nothing else. Wrap driver errors as `RepositoryError`. **No Drizzle query appears outside `src/db/`.**
- [ ] **Unit Tests** (against a temp database seeded through the real repositories, never the developer's `~/.automate`):

  - **Movement.** A task that gets a new run between page 1 and page 2 appears **at most once** across the whole traversal, and appears at the top of a fresh page 1.
  - **Filters.** Each `status` group returns exactly the tasks whose latest run is in that group; `needs_you` includes a `waiting` latest run.
  - **Search.** `q` matches the name and the prompt; `q = "50%"` matches a prompt containing `50%` and not every row; `q = "a_c"` does not match `abc`; an empty `q` applies no filter.
  - **Counts.** Five queries per page, asserted through a counting wrapper on the connection, at page sizes 1, 20, and 50.

A fully populated record, seeded through FEAT-104–109's repositories, fills every section. `inputsReadByRun` is `false` when one manifest digest differs, and `null` with no script run. `chain` links a guidance retry and a feedback re-run in both directions.

### TASK-003: The run-state invariants history relies on — restart partition, one open run per task, and "the app was closed"

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - **Restart partition.** Modify `ExecutionRepository.listActive()` to select `INTERRUPTED_ON_RESTART`, and `listParked()` to select `PARKED_STATUSES`. Modify `TaskSessionRegistry.reconcileOnStartup()` so that every `INTERRUPTED_ON_RESTART` row is marked `failed`/`EXECUTION_INTERRUPTED` with its `INTERRUPTION_MESSAGES` entry, and every `SURVIVES_RESTART` row is left exactly as it is.
    - For `waiting`, FEAT-105 already settles the pending clarification `interrupted` in the same transaction. Keep it, and assert it.
    - Every interrupted row gets its terminal `state_changed` event at the next `seq`. No event is appended for a surviving row.
    - This reverts FEAT-107 TASK-004's narrowing for `waiting` alone, and the module header names the conflict and the reason in two sentences so the next reader does not re-narrow it.
  - **One open run per task.** Add a private `assertNoOpenRun(tx, taskId)` to `ExecutionRepository`: inside the caller's transaction, it throws `TaskHasOpenRunError` when any execution of the task has a status outside `TERMINAL_STATUSES`.
    - Call it inside `createRetry` (FEAT-106's guidance retry).
    - Call it inside `createFeedbackRetry` (FEAT-107's rejection re-run) **after** the source's `awaiting_review → rejected` transition in the same transaction, so the rejected run no longer counts as open.
    - `POST /api/executions/:id/retry` needs no route change; FEAT-101's middleware renders the typed error, now mapped to 409.
  - **"The app was closed."** Thread an abort reason through the registry. `TaskSession.abort(reason: 'user' | 'shutdown' = 'user')`. `drain()` passes `'shutdown'`, and a session aborted for that reason settles `aborted` with `EXECUTION_STOPPED_ON_SHUTDOWN` and *"This run was stopped because the app was closed. Run it again to retry."* A person's own cancel still settles `aborted` with no error message, exactly as FEAT-103 specified. Without this, history labels both cases *Cancelled*, telling a person they cancelled something they did not.
- [ ] **Unit Tests**:
  - **Reconciliation.** With one execution in each of the seven non-terminal statuses: after `reconcileOnStartup`, the five `INTERRUPTED_ON_RESTART` rows read `failed`/`EXECUTION_INTERRUPTED` with their phase message, and the two `SURVIVES_RESTART` rows are unchanged field by field. The `waiting` row's clarification reads `interrupted`. Each interrupted transcript ends with a terminal `state_changed` at a gap-free `seq`, and the surviving transcripts gain nothing. Running reconciliation twice is idempotent.
  - **Retry after interruption.** A retry of the interrupted `waiting` run seeds the earlier answers through FEAT-105's `priorAnswersForTask`, asserted by `answer_source = 'seeded'`.
  - **One open run.** With the latest run at `awaiting_approval`, retrying an older failed run throws `TASK_HAS_OPEN_RUN` and creates no row, asserted by count. The same retry succeeds once the parked run is aborted. A rejection at `awaiting_review` creates exactly one feedback run. Two concurrent retry requests for one task produce one execution and one `TASK_HAS_OPEN_RUN`.
  - **Shutdown reason.** `drain` settles a live run `aborted` with `EXECUTION_STOPPED_ON_SHUTDOWN`. A user abort settles `aborted` with a null `error_code`. Both assertions sit in one test so the pair proves the distinction.
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: Invoke **Document** update mode for restart outcomes and the one-open-run rule.
- **Verify**: `pnpm --filter @automate/server test registry task-session recovery execution-repository` passes, including FEAT-103's, FEAT-105's, and FEAT-107's existing reconciliation cases, updated only where they asserted the `waiting` behavior this row corrects.

### TASK-006: Deleting a task — every row, every file, and nothing outside

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - **What a task owns on disk.** Add `src/history/task-owned-trees.ts` with `TASK_OWNED_TREES`, the five trees in §2, each as `{ kind, keyedBy: 'task' | 'execution', root: (paths) => string }`. `treesForTask(paths, taskId, executionIds)` returns every directory to remove.
  - **Safe removal.** Add `src/history/safe-remove.ts`. `removeTree(base, name)`:
    - accepts only `^\d+$` names, resolves through `resolveWithin(base, name)`, and `lstat`s the target first;
    - if the target itself is a link or junction, unlinks the link and never its target;
    - otherwise calls `fs.rm(target, { recursive: true, force: true, maxRetries: 3, retryDelay: 100 })`, which removes links inside the tree without following them;
    - treats `ENOENT` as success;
    - returns `{ removed: true }` or `{ removed: false, code }` and never throws for a filesystem error.

    Generated Python writes into `runs/{executionId}/output/` and could leave a symlink, or on Windows a junction, pointing anywhere. A delete that followed one would remove a person's files outside the data root. The tests prove this does not happen rather than assuming it.
  - **Row deletion.** Modify `TaskRepository` with `deleteOwnedRows(taskId)`. In **one transaction** it re-checks that no execution of the task is open (throwing `TaskHasOpenRunError` otherwise; a check made before the transaction could be overtaken by a retry committed in between), collects the execution ids and the run, input, and output counts, and deletes the `task` row so the cascade removes the rest. It returns `{ executionIds, counts }`. FEAT-109's file-sweep calls leave the repository; the repository no longer touches the filesystem.
  - **The service.** Add `src/history/task-deletion-service.ts`. `delete(taskId)`:
    1. `getById`, or `TaskNotFoundError`.
    2. A fast pre-check against `registry.get(executionId)` for every run, so a live session anywhere in the task refuses even if its row somehow reads terminal.
    3. `deleteOwnedRows`.
    4. **After commit**, `removeTree` for every tree in `treesForTask`.
    5. Returns `{ taskId, removed, filesPendingRemoval }`.

    **Rows first, files second** is deliberate. If files went first and the row delete then failed, the result would be live rows pointing at deleted files. With rows first, the worst case is unreferenced files, which TASK-007's sweep removes.
  - **The route.** Add `DELETE /api/tasks/:taskId` to `history-route.ts`, behind FEAT-103's `originGuard`, returning `DeleteTaskResponse`.
  - **Logging.** Log `info` `{ taskId, runs, inputs, outputs, treesRemoved, treesPending }`, and `warn` per unremoved tree with its `kind` and `code` only. **Never a task name, prompt, filename, or path.**

  - **Completeness (rows).** Drive a task through the whole pipeline with `FakeAgentProvider` and `FakePythonRunner` (uploads, consent, a clarification, two code versions, verification, approval, a run, artifacts, and a feedback re-run), then delete it. **Every table except the four global ones is empty**, asserted by enumerating `sqlite_master` rather than listing tables by hand, so a future task-owned table without a cascade fails this test.
  - **Completeness (files).** None of the five trees contains an entry for the task's or its executions' ids, and a recursive scan of the data root finds no directory named for any of them.
  - **Isolation.** A second task created alongside keeps every row and every file.
  - **Links.** A symlink (POSIX) or junction (Windows) planted in `runs/{id}/output/`, pointing at a temp directory outside the data root that holds a sentinel file: after deletion the link is gone and **the sentinel still exists**. The same holds for a link planted as `runs/{id}` itself.
  - **Contained names.** `removeTree` refuses `..`, `../x`, `5/../../x`, an absolute path, and a non-numeric name.
  - **Locked files.** When one `rm` fails with `EBUSY` (through memory's pass-through `vi.mock('node:fs/promises')` pattern), the response reports `filesPendingRemoval: 1`, the rows are still gone, and the other trees are removed.
  - **Guards.** A task with a run at `awaiting_approval` returns `TASK_HAS_OPEN_RUN` (409) and deletes nothing, asserted by row and file counts. A foreign `Origin` returns 403 before any row is read. An unknown id returns `TASK_NOT_FOUND`. A second DELETE returns `TASK_NOT_FOUND`. A retry request for a run of a just-deleted task returns `EXECUTION_NOT_FOUND`, not a 500.
  - **Log spy.** A Pino spy asserts that no log line contains the task name, a filename, or the data root.

### TASK-007: The retention sweep — interrupted deletions, crash residue, and unattached consents

- [ ] **Implementation**: Add `src/history/retention-sweeper.ts`, following the pattern of FEAT-104's `StagedUploadSweeper`: one in-flight promise shared by concurrent calls, an unref'd hourly timer, and `start`/`stop`. `sweep()` does two things:
  1. **Orphaned per-execution trees.** For each `TASK_OWNED_TREES` entry keyed by `execution`, it lists the root's entries and removes, through `removeTree`, every **numeric** entry whose id has no `execution` row. Non-numeric entries (`agent-smoke`, `connection-test-*`) are left alone. Task-keyed trees are already swept by FEAT-104 (`uploads/`) and FEAT-109 (`artifacts/`), and this sweep does not duplicate them.

     There is no race with a run being created: an execution's row is always inserted before any of its directories exist, so a directory without a row is residue, never a run in progress.
  2. **Unattached consents.** Through FEAT-105's repository, extended with `deleteUnattachedBefore(cutoff)`, it deletes `disclosure_consent` rows with `task_id IS NULL` granted more than `AUTOMATE_STAGED_UPLOAD_TTL_HOURS` ago. That is the same TTL as the staged files those consents approve. A consent attached to a task is never touched, whatever its age.

  The module header states the retention rule once (life of the task, no age-based purge) and says that this sweep is **orphan cleanup, not retention**, in the words FEAT-104's sweeper uses. Wire it into `src/index.ts` after `reconcileOnStartup` and FEAT-104's and FEAT-109's sweeps, before `listen`; then hourly; then stopped on shutdown. Log `info` with the four counts. Never log a path.
- [ ] **Unit Tests**:
  - **Orphans.** `runs/999/`, `scripts/999/`, and `agent-sessions/999/` with no execution 999 are removed; the same trees for a live execution are untouched regardless of age; `agent-sessions/connection-test-123/` and `agent-smoke/` are untouched; and a file (not a directory) named `999` is removed without error.
  - **Idempotence.** The sweep is idempotent across two runs, and two concurrent `sweep()` calls perform one sweep.
  - **Consents.** An unattached consent older than the TTL is deleted; one younger than the TTL is kept; an attached consent 90 days old is kept.
  - **Interrupted deletion.** After a simulated crash (rows deleted and `removeTree` never called), the next sweep removes all three per-execution trees, and FEAT-104's and FEAT-109's sweeps remove the two task-keyed trees. This is the test that makes "rows first, files second" safe.
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: Invoke **Document** update mode for the retention rule and the orphan sweep.
- **Verify**: `pnpm --filter @automate/server test retention-sweeper` passes; starting the server with a planted `runs/99999/` logs one orphaned run tree and removes it.
- **Depends on**: TASK-006

## 6. Cross-Cutting Concerns

- **Auth / local access (D10)**: N/A for accounts; this is a single-user local deployment (memory, D03). The protections:
  - The one new write route, `DELETE /api/tasks/:taskId`, gets FEAT-103's Origin/Host guard. This matters more for a delete than for any earlier route, because a malicious page in the person's own browser could otherwise erase their work with one request.
  - The three new reads are protected from other web pages by the same-origin policy, which holds only while no route sets a CORS header. TASK-004 therefore asserts that across every route, not just this row's.
  - `nosniff` on every `/api` response stops a browser from reinterpreting JSON.
  - None of this protects against other programs or accounts on the same machine. That is the per-install token, still open under D10 and tracked in TODO.md as a pre-pilot item. It must not be described as access control anywhere.
- **Data disclosure (D04)**: This row opens no provider session, builds no prompt, and records no transmission, as asserted in TASK-012. It *lists* the person's prompts and filenames and *summarizes* what was sent, all to the person's own browser. The record contains no payload bytes, no code, no run output, and no transcript payload. Each of those stays behind its owning feature's route, and TASK-005's sentinels prove it. **Run again** is FEAT-106's retry, which re-verifies FEAT-105's consent before sending anything.
- **Error Handling**: The one new error is `TASK_HAS_OPEN_RUN` (409), with a message that names the open run's state and the action to take; `EXECUTION_STOPPED_ON_SHUTDOWN` is a recorded outcome, not a thrown error. FEAT-101's middleware remains the only place an error body is formatted. **A file that cannot be removed is not an error.** It is counted, reported as `filesPendingRemoval`, told to the person in one sentence, and removed by the next sweep. This follows the pattern FEAT-109 set for unregistered outputs and FEAT-108 set for limit breaches. The row delete and the file removal never diverge silently.
- **Logging**: Pino. Levels:
  - `info` — a task deleted (id and counts), the retention sweep's result, and reconciliation's per-status counts.
  - `warn` — a tree not removed (its kind and errno code), a delete refused for an open run, and a retry refused for the same reason.
  - `debug` — history pages served (item count, group, `hasQuery`).

  **Never logged**: task names, prompts, search terms, guidance, review feedback, filenames, or paths. The temptation specific to this row is logging the search term or the deleted task's name "for debugging". Both are the person's words, and FEAT-103's rule covers them.
- **Performance**: Every list is keyset-paginated at memory's default of 20 and maximum of 50. Execution ids are the cursor, so no query uses `OFFSET`. A history page costs five queries at any size, and a test counts them. The run record is one small indexed query per section. Section detail loads only when opened, through lazily loaded components (memory). Polling runs only while something is running. Finished runs open no socket.
- **State recovery (plan §6)**: Every outcome is proven in TASK-012 and documented in TASK-013.
  - **Browser disconnect**: nothing is lost. History and the run view re-read the database, and a live run resumes from `lastSeq` (FEAT-103).
  - **Server restart**: `pending`, `generating`, `verifying`, `executing`, and `waiting` are interrupted, with a phase-specific message and **Run again**; `waiting`'s answers are reused (FEAT-105). `awaiting_approval` and `awaiting_review` survive and stay under **Needs you**, and their decisions still work (FEAT-107).
  - **Graceful shutdown**: live runs read *Stopped when the app closed*.
  - **Interrupted deletion**: the next startup sweep removes the residue.
  - **Another tab deleted the task**: the next read says so plainly.
- **Concurrency (D14)**: Unchanged. History reads hold no slot. Deletion refuses rather than aborting anything on the person's behalf, and the dialog offers the cancel. The one-open-run rule (TASK-003) is enforced inside the transaction that would create the second run.
- **Platform (D13)**: Windows 11 and macOS/Linux are both first-class.
  - `path.join` and `resolveWithin` are used for every path.
  - `fs.rm` gets `maxRetries` for Windows' transient `EBUSY`/`EPERM`, and a file held open by another program becomes `filesPendingRemoval` rather than a failure.
  - Link safety is tested separately for POSIX symlinks and Windows junctions, since generated code can create either without elevated rights.
  - Relative times come from `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` in the person's locale.
- **Security posture (D03)**: Unchanged, and not overstated. Deleting a task removes this application's copies of the person's data and nothing more. The unisolated Python that ran for that task could have written anywhere the server process could, and no deletion reaches that. TASK-013 requires saying so.
- **Deferred scope guard**: The following are out of scope:
  - per-run and per-artifact delete (user decision; D08);
  - a standalone artifact library, tags, or saved flags (D08);
  - consent revocation UI (TODO.md, FEAT-105);
  - task renaming;
  - full-text search;
  - any storage quota or age-based purge (D12 is a lifetime rule);
  - templates, "run against another file", and input mapping (FEAT-111);
  - scheduling (D08/D15);
  - a list-wide socket;
  - the per-install token (D10, pre-pilot);
  - any AI involvement.
- **Memory alignment**: One documented **correction** and two documented **deviations**, recorded rather than taken silently:
  - **Correction** — memory's Architecture entry says parked statuses including `waiting` survive a restart. FEAT-105's own entry, and the facts, say `waiting` does not. TASK-003 enforces the corrected partition, and TASK-013 runs the `/memorize override`.
  - **Deviation** — the `execution_parked` index and `listParked()` include `waiting`, departing from FEAT-107's spec, for the reason given in §2.
  - **Deviation** — `listActive()` reverts FEAT-107's narrowing for `waiting` only.

  Everything else follows memory as written: the repository pattern with no Drizzle outside `src/db/`; TypeBox on every input; memory's pagination defaults (applied here to a real list for the first time); Pino with its redaction rules; the typed error envelope; exact pinning (nothing new to pin); `path.join`/`resolveWithin` for every path; `ds.*` tokens with no raw Tailwind; lazily loaded heavy views; functions under forty lines; JSDoc on every public `packages/core` API; and tests under `src/__tests__/` mirroring the source tree.
